items.note: NHS: call when contractions are regular and coming every 5 minutes or more often. Measured start to start.

items.note: The NHS call-for-advice wording gives no duration, so the UK default is off (0). If a midwife gives a duration it can be set between 30 and 90 seconds.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: How long contractions must stay at the call rate before 'Time to call'. The NHS says to call when contractions are regular and every 5 minutes or more often, and gives no time, so the UK default is off (0). If a midwife asks you to wait, it can be set between 30 and 60 minutes, never longer.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: NHS: call urgently if any contraction lasts longer than 2 minutes. Can be tightened, never relaxed.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: NHS: call urgently if there are 6 or more contractions in 10 minutes. NICE defines tachysystole as more than 5 in 10 minutes, so 5 is the tightest setting.

items.note: App-defined, for midwife review. How far over the advice interval the longer gaps may run for a pattern to count as regular: with 0.35 and 5 minutes, the median gap at or under 5 minutes and three in four at or under 6:45. Also used to describe a pattern as regular or uneven.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: Only matters when a hold is set (a midwife's UK hold, or the US default): second and later babies, a previous fast labour or a journey over 30 minutes then wait at most 30 minutes. NHS: call earlier for subsequent babies and long journeys.
